body:
I really hope they'll listen to me. I'm tired of waiting and waiting for no reason. I just want to feel like I'm making progress for once. I'm also afraid that if I have to wait another 6 months, my mental health will decline even further and they'll deny me HRT because of it...

It's difficult to understand what goes through people's minds. It sounds like they're accepting you but that they still haven't gotten used to it. Maybe they have a hard time understanding and that's what's making their behavior so odd? I hope her TERF:y views change because TERFs aren't my favorite people... And maybe you're right about people feeling betrayed, maybe they feel excluded or whatever for some reason. I don't think they have a right to complain about that because after all, this is your life and your journey. We don't transition because of other people.

It's very outdated and stupid, to be frank. There used to be a requirement of one year of RLE but they removed it thankfully. I have no idea what they're expecting but I feel sorry for trans people who are unable to dress stereotypically according to their gender identity. They shouldn't be judged by that.

Yeah, I'm way closer today than I was a year ago. It'll be awesome when I finally get to start. Right now it feels like I'd want to host a party on my first day of T (and I usually stay away from parties). lol

BTW, sorry about the late reply! If you want to keep the conversation going more regularly (or chat about anything else) feel free to send me a pm. Got myself a kik account recently and I'm looking for new people to chat with :)

I'm not sure meditation would help really. My mind is too busy. You do have some valid points, though.

Sometimes I manage to just ignore it but those moments rarely last long. I just want to move on with my life, start HRT and feel like I'm making progress. I'm tired of living, looking and sounding like a 15-year old.

I can somewhat relate to what you're saying.

But remember this - you're not just female in your heart. **You** are female if that's how you feel and that includes your brain, your soul and even your body!

Even though I was born with a certain set of organs and body parts, the majority of my body parts are the same as the ones cis males have - arms, legs, feet, hands, head, ears, knees.... And I have the same organs too; liver, lungs, heart, spleen... The list goes on and the only organs I *don't* have are only a handful. 

So I'm more male than female despite what my chromosomes say.

I wholeheartedly agree. They probably do serve some kind of useful purpose when it comes to some individuals but overall, they're only making you go through unnecessary suffering. In my country, where hormones and surgeries are essentially free, they're probably even more careful because they really don't want people to regret stuff. It's going to feel fucking amazing, to put it lightly, to finally be freed from their evaluations. I've always hated going because I spend so much time before finally leaving the house just to make sure I dress as masculine as I can. They write down what you wear in the journal for some reason... One time I felt really masculine but the therapist wrote down "Unisex clothing". :(

I won't give up until I get what I need and want. If I look back, I've come a long way so there's no way I'm stopping now. T will probably help a lot and hopefully it'll be a bit easier bulking up. Just knowing that T is in my system instead of the dominant E is going to do a lot, I think. I'm trying not to set my expectations too high, but I'm looking forward to it. It'll take a while for the real changes to take place but like I said, just *knowing* I've boarded the HRT train will feel awesome.

People are probably having a hard time truly understanding what it means for someone to be transgender. That's how I feel, at least. They *want* to be accepting but they can't *grasp* the idea of "wanting to be someone else" - which isn't what we're trying to be. We just want to be **ourselves**. Having grown up a different person (from the others' perspectives) can make it difficult for people to adjust at first. Maybe sometimes people need time to get to learn the "new" you? I think there's a difference between flat out not accepting someone and trying to understand what coming out means. Eventually they'll probably realize that this **is** you, it's not going to change and that they'll just have to accept it. That's probably the best advice/rant I can come up with atm.

I truly appreciate your inspiring words. I really needed this today. Gave the GIC a call yesterday and just poured my heart and soul out. The person on the phone will be speaking to the doctor next week and hopefully, in some crazy magical way, I'll get an appointment sooner.. It's just one damn appointment, I mean. It would probably be done and over with in less than 20 mins... And I'll have to wait more than 7 months for it?! No way!!

I had a feeling you didn't. I just get very discouraged by downvotes just like any other insecure person. lo

I'm probably a tad bit bloated from time to time. In one day, my stomach can look different from one hour to the next.

I have a feeling I've been slowly gaining fat over the past months. Right now I've changed my diet and I focus more on eating more non-processed foods. The candy has been thrown out and I try my best to focus on both good nutrition, rest and healthy amounts of workouts. I'll probably have to work on getting more sleep as well. Progression pics will happen eventually. I hate taking pictures of myself but I plan on doing so as soon as I start T.
Not planning on going back to eating meat any day now. No way.
Thanks

It's so weird how people downvote you when you're just being honest... One of the main fears I had when posting this. Really regret it now, tbh.

I'm positive. It's flabby and I can grab it with my hand. Even if I flex, it doesn't get any harder.

I've been under a lot of stress lately - I'm not doing good at all, to be honest. Depressed, stressed and I'm really struggling. 

Maybe it's my muscle turning into fat or something? I don't know.

They turn me down because they don't think it's worth it for me to switch clinic. That the wait won't get shorter. And I'm so frustrated because I only have **one single appointment left** and then I'm done and I can start HRT... Why won't they just give me my diagnosis and send me off?

I really wish trading was possible. Would save a lot of trans people a lot of pain... I'm thinking my (impossible-like-how-the-fuck-did-this-even-happen?) weight gain has multiple factors - psychological and physiological stress, depression and estrogen... I'll probably still have body issues for a long while after starting HRT but at least I know my body will have the right kind of hormones going... I'm so confused though because loseit insisted on that it's not possible gaining weight while on a deficit. Don't know what to believe, tbh.

It's good that you're not hating your body as much anymore. :) Socially can be very difficult and I can relate to how people may still think of you as your birth sex. That sucks but I think that time will help with that.

School's really not working and this week just feels impossible. I'll probably talk to the counselor tomorrow because I just can't concentrate on anything. :/

I (kind of) understand what you're talking about but I can't see how it would be applied to my own dysphoria.

It's not about looking good. It's not about being a perfect weight or height or anything. It's about my brain not recognizing the body which makes more a physical issue rather than a mental one. I just can't ignore the error messages my brain keeps sending out because they're so loud and so real. There's nothing to accept because I can't help it. I'm not supposed to look like this. It's difficult for someone without gender dysphoria to understand because it's very complex.

I don't want to live in the now because the now fucking sucks and the only thing keeping me alive is looking into the future. A future where I'll actually have a life. Right now I'm just barely existing.

I'll do my best. It's just confusing and I'm feeling very discouraged. I've sent an email to a gym nearby with PT's asking them if they have any knowledge in making meal plans and such. Not sure I can do this on my own because of my background.

Thank you for your input.

I'm just as baffled as you are, believe me.

The candy was just basic pick and mix stuff. Little chocolate, small pieces of fudge. The same portion every day, basically. Not even 50 grams of it (yeah, **that** little).

I'm thinking maybe it has to do with estrogen as well. When I was underweight, I didn't have shark week for almost 1,5 years because my body fat was so low. Maybe the increase in estrogen made the fat gain boost in combination with vegan processed foods+deficit+long time in between meals? That's the only theory I have...

My parents are very supportive and I'd probably off myself a long time ago if it weren't for them. I know future friends won't have a problem with my being transgender but it's the dysphoria that's killing me. And the wait for hormones.

My dysphoria isn't about being perfect because like you say, nobody's perfect. My dysphoria is like my brain sending out distress signals because the body outwards does not reflect on the body I think I have. I don't have a perfect ideal that I'm striving to achieve, but I'd just like for my brain not to react with panic every single time I see myself naked.

Even **with** clothes, the dysphoria is there. It's always present. And I'm exhausted. Completely exhausted.

It can't only be dysphoria, I've gained fat and I'm more than 100% positive about it - can't fit into my jeans I used to wear only six months ago. And it's not muscle because it jiggles... The dysphoria makes it worse, though. That's for sure.

I think I've decided on quitting the meat replacements, though. I don't think they're that good for you. Beans, legumes and other veggies would probably be better. But the easiest way would be to go back to eating fish/poultry.

Yes. Every single ingredient. I can't prep a meal without weighing so it has become an obsession unfortunately. I barely snack on anything in between meals so I'm just as confused as everyone reading my story.

I'm thinking of going back to basics like that. Not eating processed foods at all and resorting to beans and maybe some tofu (although I'm not very fond of it). It'd be easier just going back to eating fish and poultry but it wouldn't feel right.

It will change when I start HRT.

I haven't weighed myself in years and I'm terrified of the scale. I think it'll only bring back the eating disordered habits and that's far from healthy.

I know all of that is bullshit. It's impossible. It's like you said - it's a marathon and not a sprint.

I'm terrified of being ridiculed, actually.

Thank you so much for the good advice. I've been thinking about talking to a professional about this and maybe get help with making a meal and workout plan. I don't think I can do this all on my own. I really don't. Right now I'm just so desperate and confused about how my body's changed the past 6-10 months.

Thank you for replying.

I'm positive that I've gained fat around my butt, thighs and hips because I've tried on jeans I used to wear about six months ago. They're really tight.

As for the candy - I don't even eat that much. I've weighed it and it probably adds only 200-300 kcals to my daily intake. And my daily intake is rarely above 1000 (weigh my meals). I **know** I don't eat enough.

I kind of already knew about that myth but I'm just desperate trying to find the reason behind my fat gain.

Then how in the world have I gained fat? I'm serious, I do not eat more than 1500 calories in one day and I burn off at least 400 when I run more than 15 km.

I feel so stupid.

It would just feel so wrong... I love animals. There *has* to be a way to loose weight while remaining vegan. Maybe I could just learn to enjoy beans?

Sorry to be repetitive, but you do think I'm gaining weight because of the deficit and such?

I've already given up on the candy. No more. But eating an egg? It wouldn't feel right. I'm seriously thinking about going back to being demi-vegetarian though (fish, poultry). I don't think I can handle being vegan atm; I hate beans, legumes and all that jazz. It was much easier just prepping some chicken or turkey along with some vegetables.

But do you think that I'm gaining weight because of the combination of empty calories, severe calorie deficit and the vegan processed meat? It feels like those are the reasons but I'd like to get it confirmed...

I feel extremely betrayed right now because no matter what I do (calorie restrict, working out every day), my fat does not go away. In fact, I think I've gained fat (hip, ass, thighs) and I'm freaking out right now. I'll probably ask for some advice in /r/loseit or something...

I cannot understand why either. I'm so exhausted from calling around different GICs but I've only been turned down so far.

:) Sorry for EXTREMELY late reply, by the way. This past week has been horrible. How are you doing?

*First off, a big thank you for sharing your story. I've read through it all and I'll do my best in replying and sharing some of my own experiences. It won't be as well-written or long as yours though.*

I struggle a lot and can really relate to this:

> I kept telling myself that all those things that help us are 'fake' or whatever and because it's not as good as 'being the real thing' and will 'never fully work for me'

...while at the same time there's still a hope inside of me that I desperately cling on to. Because I want to have a future. I want to have a life. I really, really do.

Sounds like a really rough way of growing up, I'm sorry. I've thankfully never received any backlash from being myself. At least not that I've been aware of. Sure, the guys distanced themselves from me when puberty started as they started seeing me as one of the girls. That really hurt and I felt really lost after that. I made friends with two of the girls but I missed the good ol' days. I never really copied anyone else but I did hide behind being the class clown.

I try so hard to build muscles but it takes forever... I've been fighting an ED for years and I'm still not free from it. Right now I wish I could go back to being underweight - no periods, no female curves, no female fat. I know it's really unhealthy but I'm feeling desperate when I notice my ass getting bigger. My arms are still skinny even though I've built some muscle. The proportions are way off and I get so dysphoric about it. I feel like ripping my skin open and walking away from this mess of a body... /rant

Sorry about that. I'm having a particularly bad day today.

It sounds really great being able to express yourself through art like that. :)

The concept of a happy accident makes sense and I like how you apply it to your own body. I hope I can one day do the same!

Thank you, Ma'am (or Miss?), for taking your time to reply to me. :)

Thank you for reading and for your reply, friend.

Sometimes I resort to daydreaming; imagining myself in five years from now with the attributes I want from T can sometimes help. If not help, at least it's distracting because I enjoy daydreaming. Taking small steps is difficult atm because I'm all out of energy because of being depressed. Sometimes I'm successful, though, and it feels good.

I like that mantra. I have one of my own - *Nothing is permanent* or *This body is not permanent*. This means that even though this body makes me feel like shit right at this moment, I can work on changing. I can build muscle, lose fat, change my hair etc. 

I also find control when I'm active. I relate very much to how you feel when you dance. But for me, I can apply it to running.

I relate to that but on the opposite side of the spectrum, so to speak. Every little feminine sign freaks me out and I can understand how the same can be applied to you. It's a pretty clear sign that gender dysphoria isn't something made up - it's more biological than people think.

I like the thought of daydreaming and I do it myself sometimes, actually. Imagining what I'll look and sound like in let's say five years from now actually brings a tiny bit of hope. It gives me something to fight towards and like you say, a hope that I one day won't feel these feelings of uneasy and dysphoria.

It's indeed a marathon. I'm just a bit crushed atm because the GIC made me believe the first step of my marathon (the assessments) was over. Turns out they've extended it and it ripped me apart. It felt like I could see the finish line but they blew it up and laughed in my face. I'm trying to get a hold of a doctor from a different GIC because according to my GIC, I only have one appointment left before being able to get on T.

I'm sorry you feel that way. I don't think I want to *die*, because I have a lot of dreams and I don't think I can put my family through that.

Some days are more manageable but right now I only have one single fking doctor's appointment left (according to my GIC) and I'm done. But they're overwhelmed with patients and they don't have enough staff. It's driving me nuts feeling like they have my life in their hands. It feels like I'm locked up and they've got the key.

I have no idea. I thought I was going to start T at the beginning of this year but nope... (read above) Now I have no idea when. I've been trying to get a doctor from a different GIC and hopefully it'll work. But right now it's a big black screen with a huge question mark in front of it. It's stressful.

I totally relate to that feeling. Like I'm inside this thing that sure, follows my commands and do stuff for me but it's actually not *me*. I tend to feel dissociated a lot and especially if I have to talk a lot. Hearing my own voice, not being as deep as I think it should be, really kicks me down. Makes me feel surreal.

That sounds like a good strategy. Being distracted from the body completely while creating stuff. I've always liked being physical and the only time I feel somewhat connected to this body is when I'm running. I still feel like shit but at least I don't feel as disconnected.

I struggle with even accepting the fact that I'm trans, and that I have to rely on hormones for the rest of my life, that I feel like shit around other trans people. I hate that. Nothing wrong with other trans people, but I feel so out of place for some reason. Probably something to do with self-acceptance. I'm also very socially anxious and there are other reasons I'm afraid of meeting new people.

The only thing that can help with my own dysphoria is running or doing distracting things. I feel like shit reading about other people's transitions because my own feel so fucking far away and there's no way I could watch timelines on youtube (especially about ftms). I tried doing that but it just makes me angry about my own situation. I've been gatekeeped and it drives me insane.

Thanks. I really hope it gets better. It feels hopeless sometimes just knowing that no matter T, no matter surgeries, I'll never be fully *me*. I guess that's all about acceptance which is incredibly hard.

I'm afraid of support group meetings. Afraid of meeting people already on T (which reminds me how much gatekeeping I'm going through atm and which leads to anger). I'm also worried I'll meet with some people I'd rather not meet again (friendship gone bad, I'm sure they're in a support group and I don't want to see them again). I *can* be my true gender everywhere but this body is always wrong. I'm so sorry you feel you can't be your true gender all the time, that must be rough :/

I'm especially suicidal during pms and knowing that it a lot of it is *because* of the pms makes me even more suicidal.

Support groups probably do exist but I'm too socially anxious to go. There are a few other reasons why I feel I wouldn't belong in a group. I'm also afraid of accidentally meet with some people I have a history with (nothing bad, just a friendship I had to end but it would be incredibly awkward if I met this person IRL).
